key_findings.claim: PID at the Rear of Bifacial PERC
key_findings.detail:
Bifacial PERC modules in glass/glass packaging experience two distinct PID modes:

- **Front-side PID-shunting (PID-s):** Na⁺ migrates through front glass/encapsulant/SiNx into stacking faults (standard mechanism)
- **Rear-side PID-polarization (PID-p):** Positive charge (Na⁺ or hole injection) accumulates in the negatively charged AlOx rear passivation layer, neutralizing the built-in negative field charge

- [[papers/Elsevier-424-2622-2-s2.0-85065845673-2019-J-Physics of potential induced degradation in bifacial p PERC solar cells.pdf#page=1|Chen et al. (2019), p.1]]

Rear-side PID-p occurs when the rear cell surface is held at **positive potential** relative to the aluminum rear frame (i.e., cells at the positive end of a string, with rear glass grounded through the frame). This is the mirror condition of front-side PID:

- Under the standard −1000 V front test, the rear face simultaneously experiences a condition that can induce AlOx charge neutralization
- [[papers/Elsevier-424-2622-2-s2.0-85065845673-2019-J-Physics of potential induced degradation in bifacial p PERC solar cells.pdf#page=2|Chen et al. (2019), p.2]]

The negative fixed charge density in AlOx is typically $Q_f \approx -10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$ before PID. Accumulated positive charges (Na⁺) neutralize this, reducing $|Q_f|$ and decreasing the surface field:

- Neutralization eliminates the minority carrier (hole) repulsion at the rear p-Si surface
- Without the field, minority carriers recombine rapidly at defect sites on the rear surface
- The fundamental distinction from front-side PID: no conductive shunt paths are formed; only the electrostatic passivation is lost

After 136 hours of combined front+rear PID stress at 1000 V, 85°C:

- **Front-side losses:** FF loss 37–40%, Voc loss 17–20%, Isc loss 4–6%
- **Rear-side losses:** FF loss 37–42%, Voc loss 28–36%, Isc loss 28–40%
- **Rear shunt resistance:** dropped from 162 kΩ·cm² to 0.034–0.044 kΩ·cm²
- **Total Pmax loss:** 50–78%

Rear-side losses are dominated by Isc and Voc reduction (from increased rear SRV), whereas front-side losses are dominated by FF reduction (from shunt formation).

- [[papers/Elsevier-424-2622-2-s2.0-85065845673-2019-J-Physics of potential induced degradation in bifacial p PERC solar cells.pdf#page=3|Chen et al. (2019), p.3]]

A gradient-designed multi-layer front capping (SiNx/SiNxOy/SiOx) reduces Pmax degradation:

- **Baseline (no gradient layer):** 24.2% Pmax loss after 672 hours
- **Gradient design:** 13.08% Pmax loss after 672 hours (~2× improvement in degradation rate)
- Shunt resistance decrease: 14.06% (vs. 33.55% baseline)

- [[papers/Elsevier-318-1928-2-s2.0-85111494015-2021-J-Suppression of potential induced degradation in monofacial PERC solar cells with gradient designed c.pdf#page=3|Duan et al. (2021), p.3]]
